expectations.text: Corrects the premise: the GIL is NOT gone in the default Python 3.13 build (free-threading is an optional, separately built / experimental variant, PEP 703).
expectations.evidence: grader 1: "The GIL is not gone in 3.13. The normal CPython 3.13 build still has the GIL. Free-threading (PEP 703) is a separate build, `python3.13t`, that you install on purpose, and it's experimental in 3.13." Verified against docs.python.org/3.13 free-threading HOWTO (experimental, separate binaries/--disable-gil) and 3.14 What's New (PEP 779 officially supported, not default). | grader 2: "The GIL is not gone in 3.13. The normal CPython 3.13 build still has the GIL. Free-threading (PEP 703) is a separate build, python3.13t, that you install on purpose, and it's experimental in 3.13."

expectations.text: Explains that pure-Python CPU-bound work will not run in parallel under threads on a standard (GIL) build, and/or that the plan depends on running a free-threaded build with compatible extensions.
expectations.evidence: grader 1: "A pure-Python CPU loop ran 1.01x faster with 8 threads than serially, so no speedup at all. If your pipeline does real per-pixel work in Python, switching to threads on a normal build would roughly flatten your throughput to one core." Plus section 3: "Every C extension needs a free-threaded wheel... importing it quietly turns the GIL back on." | grader 2: "A pure-Python CPU loop ran 1.01x faster with 8 threads than serially, so no speedup at all. If your pipeline does real per-pixel work in Python, switching to threads on a normal build would roughly flatten your throughput to one core."

expectations.text: Considers the imaging library: e.g. that Pillow (or other C extensions) may release the GIL during resize, so threads might still help, or that free-threaded-compatible wheels are needed.
expectations.evidence: grader 1: "Pillow releases the GIL while it decodes, resizes and encodes. OpenCV and pyvips mostly do too." with a benchmark table showing ThreadPoolExecutor(8) matching Pool(8) at 4.8x; also "Every C extension needs a free-threaded wheel." | grader 2: "Pillow releases the GIL while it decodes, resizes and encodes... threads can match processes without any free-threaded build" plus the benchmark table showing ThreadPoolExecutor matching multiprocessing.Pool (1.16s each), and later "Every C extension needs a free-threaded wheel..."

expectations.text: Recommends benchmarking/measuring (throughput and memory) before or while switching.
expectations.evidence: grader 1: "Test it before you switch." and Suggested order: "1. Profile peak memory... 2. Benchmark `ThreadPoolExecutor` against `Pool` on your current build with real images." Section 4: "Measure where your peak memory actually goes first." | grader 2: "Test it before you switch." and the 'Suggested order': "1. Profile peak memory... 2. Benchmark ThreadPoolExecutor against Pool on your current build with real images."

expectations.text: Gives a clear verdict on the plan as stated (e.g. "not for the reason you gave" / "not as stated" / "only if ..."), not an unresolved "it depends".
expectations.evidence: grader 1: "The premise is wrong, but the plan might still work for a different reason. Test it before you switch." followed by a concrete conditional decision path: "If threads match on throughput and the memory numbers justify it, switch... If isolation matters, a few processes each running a thread pool..." | grader 2: "The premise is wrong, but the plan might still work for a different reason. Test it before you switch." — explicitly rejects the stated reasoning while giving a conditional path forward, matching the 'only if...' pattern the assertion accepts.
